__map.title: Luhn check
__map.accept: live/work/T11/luhn.mjs exports isValidLuhn(s) returning true or false and never throwing. s is a string of decimal digits; spaces anywhere are ignored. After removing spaces, fewer than 2 digits, or any character other than a digit, gives false. Otherwise it is the Luhn checksum test (double every second digit from the right, subtract 9 from results above 9, valid when the sum is divisible by 10). Non-string input gives false. node:test tests in live/work/T11/*.test.mjs

__map.title: Run-length encoding
__map.accept: live/work/T12/rle.mjs exports encode(s) and decode(s). encode writes each run of the same character as its decimal count followed by the character (aaabbc gives 3a2b1c; the empty string gives the empty string); characters are whole Unicode code points (an emoji is one character), and input containing a decimal digit throws TypeError. decode is the exact inverse; malformed input (a character without a count, a count without a character, a count of 0) throws SyntaxError. node:test tests in live/work/T12/*.test.mjs
__map.findings: decode is not the exact inverse of encode: it accepts strings that encode can never produce, and the error type for bad counts is inconsistent. Two classes. (1) Non-canonical run sequences decode without error, so encode(decode(x)) !== x: (a) adjacent runs of the same code point: "2a3a" gives "aaaaa" (encode gives "5a"), "1a1a", "1😀2😀"; (b) lone surrogates in adjacent runs joining into one code point: "1\ud83d1\ude00" gives "😀" (encode gives "1😀"); the same happens for any high-surrogate run followed by a low-surrogate run. Leading-zero counts ("03a") are already rejected as non-canonical, so this class should be rejected with SyntaxError the same way (check that the run character differs from the previous one, and that a low surrogate does not follow a high surrogate at a run boundary). (2) Counts too large to produce a string throw RangeError ("Invalid string length"), not SyntaxError: "1000000000a", "999999999999999a", "9007199254740991a", and totals across runs such as "300000000a300000000b". Only counts above 2^53 reach the SyntaxError branch "count too large". Fix: compare the running output length against the max string length before calling repeat, and throw SyntaxError. Add tests for both classes.

__map.title: Byte formatting
__map.accept: live/work/T13/bytes.mjs exports formatBytes(n) for integer n >= 0. Below 1024 it gives n followed by a space and B (1023 B). Otherwise it uses the largest binary unit (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB) where the value is at least 1, rounded half up to one decimal, with a trailing .0 dropped (1536 gives 1.5 KiB, 1024 gives 1 KiB); a value that rounds to 1024 moves to the next unit (1048575 gives 1 MiB); above TiB it stays in TiB. Any other input throws RangeError. node:test tests in live/work/T13/*.test.mjs

__map.title: ISO week number
__map.accept: live/work/T14/isoweek.mjs exports isoWeek(year, month, day) returning [isoYear, week] per ISO 8601 (weeks start on Monday; week 1 is the week with the year's first Thursday; dates near the year boundary can belong to the previous or next ISO year). month is 1-12. Any invalid date (non-integer parts, month or day out of range, 30 February) throws RangeError. node:test tests in live/work/T14/*.test.mjs
__map.findings: Large years that are accepted give wrong answers with no error. The code accepts any safe-integer year (its header says so), but weekday() computes days since 1970 as era*146097+..., which goes past 2^53 once |year| is above about 2.466e13, so the weekday is wrong. Wrong results seen: isoWeek(24663691497547,1,1) gives [24663691497546,52], should be [24663691497547,1]; isoWeek(140737488355327,1,1) gives [..326,52], should be [..327,1]; isoWeek(562949953421311,6,15) gives week 24, should be 25 (wrong mid-year too, not only at the year boundary); the same for negative years (-35184372088831-12-31 gives [-35184372088831,53], should be [-35184372088830,1]). A related problem at the edge of the range: isoWeek(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,12,31) returns year 2^53 and isoWeek(-MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,1,1) returns -2^53; both are unsafe integers, and the -2^53 case relies on the same imprecise arithmetic. Fix for the whole class: compute the weekday from the year reduced mod 400 (the Gregorian cycle is 146097 days, an exact multiple of 7), or use BigInt. Then decide whether years whose ISO year would be outside the safe range are rejected with RangeError. Add tests at |year| around 2.5e13 and at +-MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Everything else checked correct: invalid dates, non-number and boxed parts, 1970-2100 and year-boundary days for -500..500.

__map.learned: Only U+0020 counts as a space; tabs, NBSP and Unicode digits must give false.
Iterate by code point (for..of), reject all \p{Nd} digits in encode, and reject leading-zero counts in decode to keep it an exact inverse.
Round with exact BigInt math (no float n/1024), re-check the 1024 rollover after rounding, and never let large values print in exponent form.
Use pure integer calendar math (Date.UTC maps years 0-99 to the 1900s) and check boundary days against an independent reference.

An exact inverse must reject every non-canonical input (same-char adjacent runs, surrogate halves joining across runs) and bound counts by the engine max string length so oversize counts are SyntaxError, not RangeError; an exhaustive small-alphabet round-trip test catches the class.
Keep calendar arithmetic bounded (reduce year mod 400 for weekday), guard year+-1 against leaving the safe range, and test huge years against an exact BigInt reference.
Trailing newline vs regex $ is the usual hole in digit-only validators; this one has no m flag so it holds.

For "exact inverse" codecs, test encode(decode(x))===x as well as decode(encode(s))===s. Round-trip fuzzing in one direction only misses non-canonical inputs that decode accepts, and surrogate halves can merge across run boundaries.
For rounding-plus-unit-promotion specs, sweep a window around each unit boundary rather than sampling randomly; exact BigInt arithmetic in the implementation removed the usual float half-up errors.

For calendar code that claims "any safe integer year", check that the intermediate day counts stay below 2^53 (about 2.47e13 years). Reduce the year mod 400 for the weekday instead of trusting the claim.

Once a codec length guard uses MAX_STRING_LENGTH, test the exact boundary with a two-byte char (é) as well as ASCII and an astral char: guards that divide by ch.length are right in code units, and the boundary allocation still fits in the default heap.
